Phainon was about to call it a day when his teleslate buzzed. He reached for it on the side table and turned on the screen to see a text from Stelle.

Stelle [22:57]

yo, phainon…my MVP 

my goat 

you awake 

MVP? 

Goat? 

 Really? 

He ignored it, assuming it was just another one of the strange requests the eccentric Trailblazer from beyond the sky was known for. 

His taleslate buzzed again, the screen lighting up with another text from Stelle. 

Stelle [22:58]

hey, I know you’re reading this

you need to come here  

Phainon had always thought Stelle was a little odd ever since she and Dan Heng first came to Amphoreus for the Flame-Chase journey. 

After the real Era Nova arrived and Amphoreous was finally reborn as a true world, the Astral Express had come to visit, and she had become… downright unhinged in their presence.

Whatever. He was not in the mood. 

Not tonight at least. 

Any other day, he would’ve gladly gone along with her nonsense and handled whatever ridiculous crisis she was dragging him into, but today?

No.

Because he hadn’t seen Mydei.

His Mydei had ghosted him the whole day. They didn’t spar, they didn’t unwind in the baths, and when Phainon texted him, his teleslate was out of service. He wasn’t in his chambers either, and none of the other heirs had the faintest clue where he’d gone.

Only Titans knew where that blond menace had run off to.

Though they had parted ways just last night after a very… refreshing bath, Phainon was already in the depths of withdrawal. It had been 18 hours and 36 minutes—37 now—since he’d last seen the crown prince.

Stelle [22:59]

he's drunk outta his mind 

take him away 

please

Stelle [23:00]

he’s also very pauwdhdhdkfnropwlajdhforek

Phainon stared at that last message.

…What?

His teleslate dinged with an image.

He opened it to find a blurry, extreme close-up of… pouty lips.

What the fuck! 

What was wrong with her? 

First, why was Stelle texting him about some random dude who's drunk? 

Second, what was that weird-ass last message supposed to be?

Third, why did she send him a blurry picture of someone’s lips? 

Phainon swore Stelle must have been dropped on the head as a child. 

Yep, that's it. That's the only reasonable explanation. 

Still… there was something about those lips.

Something familiar.

Something that tugged at the part of him that was hopelessly soft for one particular blond.

Oh Mydei.

His beloved.

His adorable little lion.

He missed him so much it physically hurt.

He was about to switch off the teleslate and wallow in his Mydei-inflicted misery when it buzzed again.

Phainon almost switched it off, but the new message made him freeze.

Stelle [23:04]

Deliverertyyf misss yio 

Phainon’s eyes widened. There was only one person in the entire cosmos who called him by that nickname.

Mydei.

Mydei was the one texting him.

Mydei missed him.

Phainon smiled.

But hold on.

If Mydei was texting him from Stelle’s teleslate…

… that meant he was with her. This whole time? Time he could’ve spent with Phainon?

Phainon frowned.

Then again, this could be a trap. He thought.

Stelle knew he’d come running anywhere if Mydei was involved. He was “down bad” for the blond, as the Trailblazer had eloquently put it once. 

He was still debating in his head whether or not this was Stelle impersonating Mydei when his teleslate rang with an incoming video call. Without thinking twice, he accepted. 

The first thing he saw was a blur of something. Of what? He couldn't say, because it was, well, blurry.

He heard Stelle’s voice in the background, saying something like ‘give it back.’

Then a very, very familiar voice say ‘no’, dragging out the syllable. 

The screen jolted and wobbled for a bit, before finally getting into focus. 

Phainon could not believe his eyes. 

On the tiny pixelated screen, he saw the greatest thing he's ever seen.

Unruly golden hair, cheeks as red as the ripest pomegranates, glassy amber eyes, and luscious pink lips—glossy with either spit or whatever he’d been drinking—filled the entire frame.

“Mydei?” Phainon squeaked.

Mydei squinted at the camera as if it had personally insulted his entire bloodline. His eyes were a little red, eyelids drooping, and he swayed so much that the screen dipped every other second.

“Deliv’rer…” Mydei slurred, voice thick and warm like melted honey. 

“Why’re you… why’re you textin’ the Trailblazer… this late at night?”

He jabbed a finger toward the camera, missing it completely. 

“This late. At. Night,” he repeated, every word coming out slower, heavier, like his mouth had forgotten how speech worked.

In the background, Stelle groaned. “He’s been asking that for ten minutes, Phainon. Ten. Straight. Minutes.”

Mydei ignored her, leaning closer until the screen was just a blur of golden eyes and flushed cheeks. 

“You shouldn’… you shou—shouldn’t be talking to other people,” he mumbled, trying to focus. 

“Especially not her. She’s… she’s loud. And she makes bad jokes. And she threw… threw a chair at me.”

“I did NOT!” Stelle shrieked.

“You t-tried,” Mydei corrected, before turning back to the screen. 

“Only because you ripped my hair off when you saw me texting ‘Your Deliverer’,” she shot back.

“Deliv’rer.” He hiccuped, ignoring the gray-haired girl. 

“D–Don’ talk to her,” Mydei slurred. “She wants youuu.”

Behind him, Stelle let out an offended gasp.

“Ew. I do NOT want him,” Stelle snapped.

Okay—no need to sound so offended. Phainon didn’t want her either. 

“You want everyone!” Mydei shot back.

Phainon let out a slow breath, clearly done with this entire conversation, “She doesn't want me. Now, Mydei, where are you?” 

At that, Mydei leaned so close his nose smushed the camera. His voice dropped to a pouty, whispering complaint, promptly ignoring Phainon's question. 

“You talk to me. Not… not her or anyone else. 

Another hiccup. “Me. Only. Me.”

In the background, Stelle muttered something about needing hazard pay.

“Mydei, I am talking to you.” 

Phainon huffed, “and I was only talking to Stelle because she reached out to me. For you. And I’ve been trying to text you all day. Your teleslate was off.”

“Oh? It was tired,” Mydei said confidently.

“...come again?”

“Tired,” Mydei said, nodding solemnly. “It needed a break.”

Phainon blinked. “A break?”

It’s been carryin’ my messages for months so I just left it in the baths to relax.”

He smiled, so proud, so drunk, so stupidly adorable Phainon wanted to bite something, preferably him.

Phainon put his face in his hand and groaned. No wonder he had been unable to reach him all day. 

“Mydei… where are you?”

Mydei didn’t reply, he stared at the screen for some time. And then very softly, with the earnestness of a man too drunk to lie, he said

“… missssssed you.”

Phainon’s heart melted. Maybe Mydei should drink every day if it meant him being this adorable and honest. 

Stelle pointed at him, yelling, “he's been saying that too. Please come get him. He is also very handsy. Even Mr. Yang’s getting embarrassed."

“I liiike his… glasses… an’ h—his musclesss,” Mydei mumbled.

Glasses? Muscles? What?  

The screen lurched again—this time showing Mydei collapsing sideways into a man. 

A well-built, muscular man. 

Mydei let out a dramatic, drunken sigh as he landed against him, cheek smushed into the man’s shoulder.

Phainon couldn’t see the man’s face, but he didn’t need to. This had to be the infamous Welt Yang, one of the members of the Astral Express crew.

A spike of irritation shot through him.

How dare this guy have a physique Mydei likes.

Mydei should only like his muscles.

Only Phainon's..

And glasses—was that Mydei’s thing now? 

Phainon could wear glasses. He’d look better in glasses. He’d look amazing in glasses. 

Way better than that man. 

Welt could choke.

“D’liv’rer…” Mydei whined, successfully yanking Phainon out of his spiraling jealousy.

“Loooook… lookit his… his muscles."

He turned the camera toward the man’s arm. More like waved it wildly until it finally landed on the target.

Phainon watched in frozen horror as Mydei’s free hand drifted toward the man's bicep. Mydei missed the first time, tried again, then latched on with the determination of a drunk toddler grabbing a toy.

“Mmmmmm…” Mydei hummed, eyes half-lidded. 

“V’ry… sturrrdy… an’ thiiiick.”

He squeezed again for emphasis.

Phainon almost screamed, but he didn’t. 

No—he couldn’t. 

He had to preserve his dignity. He absolutely refused to embarrass himself in front of that… that Welt.

“STELLE,” Phainon barked at the screen, hoping the girl was close enough to hear him through the chaos.

He grimaced as Mydei continued happily ogling Welt, poking his bicep like it was the most fascinating object in the universe. 

Then suddenly, the screen jerked, the teleslate ripped from the drunk blond’s hands.

“Please get your loverboy. I beg you, Phainon,” Stelle's panicked face filled the view, her gray hair unruly and sticking out in all directions, probably because Mydei had tried to rip half of it out.

“I will do anything. Just get him… away from here—”

She glanced off-screen and visibly gagged. “And away from Mr. Yang. Especially from Mr. Yang.”

A muffled, drunken “Ooh… can I touch ‘er thighs,” echoed in the background.

Phainon clenched his jaw so hard it could’ve cracked. 

“Keep an eye on him,” he said through gritted teeth. “I’ll be right there.”

                                     《♡》

Phainon didn’t bother changing. He didn’t bother fixing his hair. He didn’t even bother grabbing his coat.

He simply grabbed his teleslate and marched out of his chambers like a man possessed.

Every step echoed with one repeating thought.

Welt Yang. 

His muscles.

Mydei touched his muscles.

Phainon quickened his pace.

By the time he reached the bar where Stelle said they were, he didn’t even have to ask if he’d found the right place, he could hear it.

“Stelleeee, lemme goooo— I wanna see his— muscles!”

“No! Mydei, stop trying to take Welt’s coat off! Welt, don't help him!”

Phainon burst in.

The scene stopped like a paused drama.

Stelle had both arms wrapped around Mydei’s waist, digging her boots into the floor as he leaned forward, trying to take off the coat of a… very good-looking gentleman with glasses and dark hair.

“Mydeimos,” Phainon said. 

Mydei turned at the sound. 

His entire face lit up.

“D—Delivere’rrr!” he cried, arms flailing. 

He instantly abandoned the stranger’s coat, thank the Titans, and staggered toward Phainon. Stelle let go the moment she felt the tension leave Mydei’s body and collapsed onto a chair with a melodramatic groan.

“He’s your problem now.”

Mydei half-ran, half-tripped straight into Phainon’s chest.

He tried to cling, really tried, but before he could tackle Phainon into a full-force hug, the white-haired man’s arms shot out, grabbing the blond by the shoulders and holding him upright at a distance.

The blond pouted at being denied the hug and started making grabby hands towards phainon. 

Phainon almost cooed at the heart-stopping, adorable sight, but priorities came first. He needed to do a damage assessment before indulging in his cuteness.

“Mydeimos of Castrum Kremnos,” Phainon said, voice dropping into that terrifyingly calm tone that meant danger.

“Why did you drink? Since when do you drink? And more importantly—” he leaned in, eyes narrowing, “—who thought you plus alcohol was a good idea?”

Mydei blinked at him. Slowly. Like he'd just been asked to do calculus.

Then his gaze wandered around the bar, unfocused and drifting, before landing on a certain gray-haired girl.

Mydei lifted a hand, missed the direction entirely, corrected it, then announced. 

“SHE did. She got me drunk.”

He jabbed a thumb toward Stelle.

Stelle went rigid. 

“Wh— I— that—” Stelle pointed at herself, utterly horrified. 

“I did not! Okay—okay, maybe I did a little, but he kept saying he could ‘handle it,’ and then he got drunk off a single glass of wine! A single glass! So, technically he’s the one at fault here.”

Mydei shook his head at that, clearly denying the Trailblazer’s explanation. 

He huffed, crossing his arms, pushing his … very generous pecs together, that looked even more plump and enticing now that they were squished. 

And oh, Phainon was distracted.  

“Deliverer, it’s not my fault. She got me drunk.”

“Hey! You are the—” 

“Yep! I-I didn’t even wanna come. She drrrrragged me.”  

Eh? 

What was Mydei saying again? 

“And then… she told me that she’ll introduce me to a great man,” Mydei continued. 

Phainon snapped out of the chest-induced haze so fast he nearly sprained something.

No matter how indecently plump Mydei’s pecs looked…

No matter how red his nipples were from being smushed…

He needed to focus.

“An’ she said I should come say hi—“

“Mydei, stop!“

“—to the hot daddy from the Express and make him notice me.”

A chorus of “What?!” echoed in the bar, as both Phainon and Welt immediately turned to look at the girl. 

Mydei, blissfully unaware, smiled proudly, certain he had provided an important, helpful piece of information.

Stelle let out the most strangled noise known to humankind.

“Why would you even say that out loud?” 

She squeaked, glancing at Welt before her shoulders slumped and her eyes went wide. 

In that moment, she resembled a raccoon caught digging through a dumpster; wide-eyed, guilty, and absolutely ready to bolt.

Phainon looked one second away from committing a crime of passion.

And Welt, standing off to the side, just closed his eyes, pinched the bridge of his nose, and muttered, “I should have stayed on the Express.”

Then, to his credit, he raised both hands in a peaceful gesture. “Alright. Let’s all take a breath. There’s no need for this to escalate—”

Phainon’s glare shut him up immediately. Welt’s hands lowered. His mouth closed.

Stelle remained frozen, wisely choosing silence.

And Phainon was done.

Still holding Mydei firmly by the shoulders, he turned the blond around and started steering him toward the exit. 

“No need. We are leaving.”

Mydei let himself be guided, feet shuffling obediently as Phainon pushed him forward. 

“Okaaay…” he murmured, leaning heavily into Phainon’s hold.

They were halfway to the door when Mydei twisted around as much as Phainon’s hold allowed. He lifted one arm in a sloppy wave.

“Bye bye, hot daddy!”

Welt dropped his cane.

Stelle looked like she might spontaneously combust.

Phainon just pushed Mydei out faster. 

                                    《♡》

Phainon’s house from the bar was only ten minutes away, but they had been walking for twenty.

Because Mydei kept wandering off the path like he’d forgotten how to walk in a straight line.

And Phainon had had enough. It had been a long night.

First, he hadn’t seen Mydei the entire day.

Then, he found out the blond apparently had the hots for an older man with glasses from beyond the sky.

Phainon stopped in his tracks.

He didn’t speak. He simply reached out, and grabbed Mydei by the waist, fully prepared to toss him over his shoulder, carry him home, and be done with the night.

But Mydei shrieked at his touch like he was being murdered.

“NOOOOOOO!”

Phainon jerked back, stunned.

Mydei… didn’t want him touching him?

The thought hit like a blade, clean and merciless. Sharp little stabs shot through his chest, dragging him straight into that terrible, familiar spiral—

When Mydei leaned forward and wrapped both arms snugly around Phainon’s neck.

The familiar scent of his vanilla bath oil washed over him, soft and warm, blended with something citrusy, probably the alcohol.

Phainon froze as Mydei’s arms tightened around his neck, the warmth of him pressing close. He was so close that every time Mydei exhaled, his warm breath brushed against his cheek.

Phainon went completely still.

Mydei’s breath brushed his cheek, warm and faintly ticklish. His body fit into Phainon’s as if he’d done it a thousand times before.

“…Mydei?” Phainon managed, voice dropping into something embarrassingly low.

“Deliv’rer,” he mumbled, melting into him, “‘m tired.”

Phainon’s hand lifted on its own, sliding around Mydei’s back to steady him. Mydei immediately relaxed further, sighing softly, like being held by Phainon was a relief.

“We are almost there. Just walk a bit more, hm,” Phainon said, voice coming out far softer than he intended.

Mydei didn’t move.

Instead, he just fluttered his long lashes, almost shyly, “…carry me?”

Phainon blinked. “I was going to carry you… before you pushed me.”

“Nooo…” Mydei tilted his head back, eyes glassy and pleading.

“Not like that. Carry me like—”

He made a vague swooping gesture, nearly smacking Phainon in the face, “—like a… a princess…”

Phainon just stared at him.

Mydei gazed back, adorable and hopelessly drunk, still clinging to him like he was something precious.

Phainon’s heart gave an undignified lurch.

And he folded like a lawn chair.

“…You’re unbelievable,” he whispered, but his arms were already moving to lift him.

Phainon shifted his grip, one arm sliding beneath Mydei’s knees, the other supporting his back. Mydei let out a soft, delighted gasp as Phainon lifted him clean off the ground.

Mydei weighed practically nothing like this, all soft and pliant, trusting every step to him.

“There,” Phainon muttered, adjusting the blond against his chest. “This okay for you? Or should I commit fully and call you my princess too?”

Mydei froze instantly, eyes going wide as crimson bloomed across his cheeks. He buried his face into Phainon’s shoulder, clearly trying to disappear. 

Phainon felt a small, sharp thrill at the sight. He just wanted to tease his Mydei, but seeing him like this… flustered, vulnerable, and utterly helpless… something inside him stirred, sharp and insistent.

His cock twitched in his pants. 

“Mmm yes,” came Mydei’s muffled whisper, his mouth pressed to Phainon’s shoulder so the sound vibrated straight through him. “Perfect…”

Phainon started walking, wearing the dumbest, happiest smile because he was carrying the love of his life in his arms.

He made it all of three steps.

Then he nearly face-planted. 

Because the strangest thing happened.

Mydei… giggled.

Mydeimos.

The crown prince of Castrum Kremnos.

The Lance of Fury.

Giggled.

Like a blushing maiden.

Heavens above.

He giggled.

Phainon looked down, and nearly forgot how to breathe.

Mydei was softly laughing, pearly teeth on full display, face, neck, and even his bare shoulders flushed the prettiest shade of pink. His eyes shimmered, half-lidded and bright, and he clutched Phainon just a little tighter.

“You are sooo strong,” Mydei sighed dreamily, staring up at him with actual stars in his eyes.

Phainon opened his mouth to say something, probably something snarky like ‘obviously since he was the only one capable of keeping up with Mydei.’ 

Only the drunken menace was not done.

“And, I like your muscles more…” he added, voice hushed like he was sharing the universe’s greatest secret.

Phainon nearly dropped him. 

But, a teeny-tiny voice inside his head whispered, ‘Take that, Welt.’ 

“Mydei—!” he choked.

Mydei just stared up at him, cheeks flushed, and eyes sparkling, reflecting the stars above. 

“Mm-hm,” Mydei continued dreamily, pawing Phainon’s chest like a sleepy kitten. 

“They’re nice, warm, and… hard.”

Phainon made a sound that could not be translated into any known language.

He tried to keep walking, but his legs weren’t working right, mostly because his brain had stopped working entirely.

However, Mydei kept talking, blissfully unaware he was causing heart palpitations.

“You know what else is hard?” he whispered, caressing Phainon's chest.

Phainon felt his blood rush south in an instant, a flush spreading through him like wildfire.

Okay, so drunk Mydei was a bit pervy.

Phainon was cool with that. 

Absolutely chill. 

Zero complaints.  

Did he say things like that to Welt too? His mind, his own worst enemy, unhelpfully added. 

His stomach plummeted.

Phainon was not cool with that.

Mydei swayed in his arms, smiling innocently and glassy-eyed, his hands continuing their assault on Phainon’s chest. 

Phainon silently cursed himself for abandoning his coat. With only a thin undershirt between them, he could feel the searing heat of Mydei’s palm burning through the fabric.

To make matters worse, Mydei’s whole body was as hot as a furnace and all Phainon wanted to do was sink into him. 

Figuratively and literally. 

“Swords…,” Mydei slurred, “they are hard.” 

Phainon sighed in relief.

Oh, his Mydei was not pervy. He was sweet, innocent and could do nothing wrong. Anyone who thought otherwise would catch these hands.

Mydei tightened his arms around Phainon’s neck, pulling him closer, his breath warm and sweet with alcohol.

“An’ you—Deliverer—are packin’ one hell of a sword.”

And then he started giggling, like he hadn’t just dropped a line that could level a grown man. A soft, delighted little laugh, as if he’d made a joke about tiny chimeras, and not… that.

Phainon blinked, brain short-circuiting.

“Mydei,” he said weakly, “stop. You’re killing me.”

Mydei giggled again, nuzzling into him. “Nooo… I want you to kill me… with that long and thick sword of yours.”

Scratch that.

Mydei was a pervy drunk.

A shameless, devastatingly adorable, absolutely lethal pervy drunk.

But he would still body-slam anyone who dared insult his beloved. 

Phainon, red to the ears and heart pounding like a war drum, forced himself to move forward again. 

This was a divine trial of his restraint, one the Aeons clearly designed for their own entertainment. Every breath Mydei puffed against his shoulder, every drunken giggle, every ridiculous innuendo felt like a slap to his self-control.

If Phainon survived this night, he deserved an award.

“Stab me, Deliverer. With those nine inches of yours.” The blond wheezed. 

Yeah, Phainon definitely deserved an award. 

Mydei surprisingly went quiet after that, simply staring at Phainon. His gaze didn’t waver, didn’t even flicker. He just… watched him.

Phainon was happy with that. More than happy. Mydei could stare at him all he wanted for as long as he wanted, and he would gladly bask in it. 

After a few long minutes of silence, he shifted in Phainon’s arms and smiled that soft, dazed little smile that always managed to hit Phainon right in the chest. 

And thus began Round 3 of ‘Can Phainon Survive This?’ 

“You know…” Mydei started, voice warm and lazy, “your stamina is formidable, Deliverer.”

Phainon nearly missed a step. “Wh—what?”

Mydei nodded sagely, as if delivering ancient wisdom.

“When we first met… we fought for ten nights and ten days straight.”

His fingers absentmindedly traced Phainon’s collar. “No food, no rest, no surrender… and we still didn’t break each other.”

Phainon swallowed hard. “…Yes. I remember.”

“My immortality helps me power through,” Mydei continued, “but you…”

He poked Phainon’s chest, eyes half-lidded but sharp with admiration.

“You kept up with me without immortality. Without divine reserves. Just sheer will and power.”

“…Where are you going with that—”

“And that makes me wonder…”

Mydei leaned in, voice dropping into a slow, sinful whisper right against Phainon’s ear.

“—just how much of a beast you are in bed.”

Phainon stopped walking so abruptly that Mydei bounced in his arms.

He stared straight ahead, face blank, expression frozen, soul leaving his body like smoke drifting into the astral plane.

“Mydei—”

His voice cracked.

Mydei giggled, delighted. “It’s true! If you can last ten days fighting me… imagine—”

“Stop talking.”

Mydei only grinned wider, absolutely drunk, absolutely honest, absolutely destructive. 

Then he did something that Phainon could not have foreseen in a million years. 

Mydei shifted in his arms again, slowly this time, deliberately, lifted his face, and pressed his lips to the spot just beneath his jaw, soft and warm.

To make matters worse, he nipped at the skin with his sharp teeth, flicked out his tongue to lick the spot, and then blew on it.

And just like that Phainon.exe crashed. 

Titans have mercy. 

He was hard. 

Painfully so.  

In the middle of the street. 

Like a pervert. 

While carrying a very drunk, very attractive prince, who also happened to be the love of his life, back to his quarters. 

Mydei, with all the regal confidence of a drunk deity making terrible decisions, placed a hand on Phainon’s cheek.

“Let’s copulate,” he announced cheerfully, nodding to himself, proud of his vocabulary choice.

“Yes. Copulate. Engage in a mutually enthusiastic physical union.”

Mydei lifted one hand and curled his fingers into a loose circle.

Then, he took his other hand, pointed one finger straight out—

—and began poking it rhythmically through the circle.

“Sex, Deliverer,” he announced, “let's have sex.” 

Phainon ran.

With Mydei nestled in his arms, mind you. He'd never leave his princess—

prince, alone in that state. 

After all, they were in the middle of a public street.

A dead-quiet, empty-at-this-hour street, sure, but still a public place.

He couldn’t let anyone see him walking around with Mydei in his arms and a tent in his pants. 

Phainon didn’t know how long he ran, but he didn’t slow down until he reached the door of his quarters. He shouldered open the door and stumbled inside, breathless. Only once the door slammed shut behind him did he dare stop.

He bent over slightly, still clutching Mydei, lungs burning, and inadvertently made eye contact with the man in his arms, who was wide-eyed, red-faced, and breathless, as if he had been the one running.

But there was something else flickering in those glassy eyes.

Oh.

Oh no.

Phainon recognized that look instantly.

Hunger.

Want.

Raw, unfiltered desire.

Phainon knew it well, because he had been looking at Mydei like that for years.

His gaze dropped involuntarily to the blond’s lips, soft and slightly parted. Mydei’s pink tongue darted out, licking at them lazily, and Phainon’s heart skipped a beat.

The world shrank until it was just him, Mydei, and that electric, dangerous hunger, radiating between them. His knees threatened to give out, and he realized with a sharp, panicked clarity that he was utterly and catastrophically undone.

Before he could do something he would regret later, Phainon decided to put Mydei to bed.  

He could take care of the throbbing ache between his legs later, in private, to the thoughts of this unhinged, clingy, sexy, chaotic, pervy version of Mydei. Later.

But for now…

He stepped toward the bed, intending to set the drunk man down gently— but Mydei, ever the unpredictable— acted faster. With a sudden, mischievous lunge, he wrapped his arms around Phainon’s neck and yanked him forward.
